newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer offers merger to Bre-X.
newsitem.headline: Placer offers merger to Bre-X.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc said on Tuesday it has presented a merger proposal to Bre-X Minerals Ltd, majority holder of the massive Busang gold deposit in Indonesia.

The Placer proposal, which was sent to Bre-X president chief executive David Walsh from Placer president and chief executive John Willson in a letter dated January 13, will offer the Indonesian government participation of up to a 40 percent equity interest in the Busang project.
It contemplates a stock-for-stock "merger of equals" at a "significant" premium to Bre-X's current share price.

Under Placer's proposal, the mining giant would initiate the staged construction of a Busang mine and plant of up to 200,000 tonnes per day costing up to US$1.7 billion. Gold production would start in 1999 and would average about three to four million ounces a year.

The plan is subject to negotiation with Bre-X and the Indonesian government, due diligence, issuance of a contract of work (COW) for the project, resolution of all ownership issues and regulatory and shareholder approval, Placer said.
Willson said in the letter that Placer and Bre-X have been in continuous talks about a venture since October 1996.

"In October, you expressed interest in such a business combination, yet for various reasons, you indicated you were not able to give such a transaction serious consideration," Willson said in the letter.

"In light of the Barrick Gold proposal and the substantial uncertainty as to its implications for your shareholders, and our continuing strong interest in Busang, we are presenting this proposal now so that you and your board can fully evaluate the potential benefits this proposal provides to Bre-X shareholders," he added.

Placer said it would like to begin negotiations immediately to create a tax-effective, stock-for-stock "merger-of-equals" under which all of Bre-X's shares would be exchanged for a fixed number of Placer shares.
The Indonesian government is currently considering a joint venture proposal from Bre-X and Canadian gold giant Barrick Gold Corp, the partner the government selected for Bre-X.
The government has said it wants a deal that would split the richest part of the Busang deposit with 67.5 percent going to Barrick, 22.5 percent to Bre-X and 10 percent to Indonesia.
